mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) drop of more than 10% in the same month indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST < previous month - 10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly below zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) increase above 0.4 percentage points from the prior month, sustained for two consecutive months, signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which pressure corporate margins and lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly different from zero during triggered periods at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces input demand and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month - 0.5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 30% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically negative at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly decline in the effective federal funds rate below 1% during a recession (UNRATE > 6%) signals an aggressive easing cycle, which lowers risk-free rates and boosts equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly above zero during triggered episodes at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) of more than 5% from the prior month, sustained for two consecutive months, indicates households are saving more and spending less, which reduces demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > previous month + 5% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered periods at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and payroll employment (PAYEMS) month-over-month is impossible; however, a large drop in PAYEMS alongside a rise in UNRATE exceeding 0.3pp signals significant labor market churning and weakness, which depresses earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.3pp AND PAYEMS falls > 0.5% month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly below zero during triggered episodes at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the housing starts index (HOUST) of at least 5% for four consecutive months signals a robust residential construction cycle, which boosts demand for materials and services and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > previous month + 5% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly above zero during triggered periods at 90% confidence.
